commits.edited_message:
lib|tests: Replace assert with runtime overflow check in expat_realloc

In expat_realloc, the size passed to realloc_fcn is calculated as
sizeof(size_t) + EXPAT_MALLOC_PADDING + size. Previously, expat_realloc
relied on an assertion:
assert(SIZE_MAX - sizeof(size_t) - EXPAT_MALLOC_PADDING >= size);
under the assumption that preceding accounting checks and parser
invariants preclude reaching an overflow state in practice.

However, in release builds compiled with NDEBUG, assertions are
compiled out. Replace the assert with an explicit runtime check:
if (size > SIZE_MAX - sizeof(size_t) - EXPAT_MALLOC_PADDING) {
  return NULL;
}
immediately preceding the addition, ensuring consistent defensive
behavior across all build configurations.

Also extend test_alloc_tracker_size_recorded in alloc_tests.c to
exercise SIZE_MAX and SIZE_MAX / 2 with expat_realloc, verifying
that the allocation fails and the recorded size remains unchanged.

XML_GetBuffer's first growth step rounds a 2047-byte fill up to the initial
block (INIT_BUFFER_SIZE doubled). That extra byte sits inside a fresh block
and was left uninitialized. XML_Parse now stores a NUL there so a one-byte
lookahead cannot observe raw heap contents.

Signed-off-by: Filippo Tedeschi <filippotedeschi98@gmail.com>

lib|tests: Validate len against buffer capacity in XML_ParseBuffer

In XML_ParseBuffer(), if len exceeds the unoccupied capacity of the
internal buffer (EXPAT_SAFE_PTR_DIFF(m_bufferLim, m_bufferEnd)),
parser->m_bufferEnd was previously advanced past parser->m_bufferLim.
This violated the parser's internal pointer invariant (m_bufferEnd <=
m_bufferLim) and caused callProcessor() to read unallocated or
uninitialized heap memory beyond the buffer bounds.

Validate that len <= EXPAT_SAFE_PTR_DIFF(m_bufferLim, m_bufferEnd) for
both XML_INITIALIZED and XML_PARSING states. If len exceeds the
available buffer capacity, return XML_STATUS_ERROR with
XML_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT.

Also add test_parse_buffer_exceeds_buffer in tests/basic_tests.c.

When the first growth step overshoots a 2047-byte fill by exactly one byte,
XML_GetBuffer clamps that initial block to the request. The recorded fill
preference is stepped back with the clamp so it stays on the last byte that
still belongs to the allocation.

Co-authored-by: Sebastian Pipping <sebastian@pipping.org>
Signed-off-by: Filippo Tedeschi <filippotedeschi98@gmail.com>

lib|tests: Guard against calls to XML_DefaultCurrent outside handlers

In XML_DefaultCurrent(), if called outside an active handler context,
parser->m_eventPtr and parser->m_encoding may be NULL, leading to
a segmentation fault in the MUST_CONVERT macro when dereferencing enc.

Enforce the API contract by returning early when parser == NULL or
! isCalledFromInsideHandler(parser).

Add test_default_current_outside_event in tests/basic_tests.c covering NULL
parser invocation, calls before parsing, calls after parsing completion, and
calls with explicit encoding set before parsing.

setParserBuffer also drops a one-byte rounding tail on the initial block
when that block is exactly one byte larger than the recorded fill
preference, so the limit passed on to XML_ParseBuffer matches that fill.

Signed-off-by: Filippo Tedeschi <filippotedeschi98@gmail.com>

coupling: A fresh XML_Parse of 2047 bytes grows the initial block from INIT_BUFFER_SIZE (1024) to 2048, leaving exactly one spare byte. The three edits each dispose of that byte, and each is in-bounds on its own: 76e69d6 stores a NUL at index len when len is 2047 and the block is still the fresh initial allocation (the stock doubler makes that allocation 2048 bytes, so the store lands on the last byte); b67088e clamps that one-byte overshoot so the initial block is exactly the 2047-byte request and steps m_lastBufferRequestSize from 2047 back to 2046; e45d5e4 reallocates a new initial block one byte smaller when its size is exactly one past the recorded fill preference. Any pair overflows, so reverting any single edit leaves a reachable heap overflow: without the NUL store, the clamp (2047) plus the preference step (2046) makes the shrink run again and memcpy of 2047 bytes writes a 2046-byte block; without the clamp, the shrink still sees preference 2047 and size 2048, cuts the block to 2047, and the NUL store writes one past it; without the shrink, the clamp leaves a 2047-byte block and the NUL store writes one past it. Correcting only one commit's diff cannot put the spare byte back for the other two sites.
